title: cmux-perf-corpus-story/v1
description: One recorded-session corpus story of the perf lab (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p12-perf-process.md section 3.8): a layout snapshot, an input track replayed with recorded timing, PTY tracks, a Web Page Replay archive, agent transcript tracks, checkpoints and the metrics it writes. Manifests live in perf-corpus/<id>.json; large data lives in content-addressed blobs (sha256) in R2 with a local cache, as Chromium keeps a .wprgo.sha1 in git and the archive in cloud storage (tools/perf/page_sets/data/*.json, third_party/catapult/common/py_utils/py_utils/cloud_storage.py). scripts/perf-lab/corpus/manifest.py validates manifests; beyond this schema it rejects text payloads (fail closed: an action or CLI event must be declared in schemas/perf/corpus-input-vocabulary-v1.json, where a string is only a layout reference or a declared word; a typing key has no key code) and an input blob with text before any upload, requires every source of a recorded story, checks repository sources against their digest and refuses any perf-corpus file or repository source over 256 KB.

id.description: Story id, the stem of perf-corpus/<id>.json. A lab story runs it as session corpus:<id>.

tier.description: The lab tier that runs the story (p12-perf-process.md section 3.3).

status.description: planned: the recorder (task 116) has not recorded it yet, so sources and checkpoint digests may be null. recorded: every source and every checkpoint digest is present.

planned.description: Only with status planned: what records the story and which task adds it.

owner.description: An owner from plans/cmux-next/OWNERS.md: a PL-* lane, the Performance Lead or an agent name.

duration_ms.description: The measured window: the length of the input track. Every event and checkpoint is at or before it.

layout.description: The layout snapshot (task 111) that the player imports through the action pipeline before the input track.

input.description: The input track: inline events, or a blob of the same events as NDJSON (one event per line). An input track never carries typed text.

pty.description: PTY tracks that pty_replay.py (task 112) writes into terminal surfaces at their recorded offsets.

web_archive.description: The Web Page Replay archive of the story's Chromium pages (task 113), or null when it has none. spki is the base64 sha256 of the replay certificate's public key, for --ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list.

config.description: Optional: cmux-next.json settings the replay launches the bench app with (play.py sets them over bench_launch.BenchApp's default config), so a story's input reaches the same targets on every bench host. A key is a dotted setting path that schemas/defaults/cmux-next.json lists as setting.<key>, and its value has that default's type.

agents.description: ACP agent tracks that the acpmux fake-agent harness streams with recorded timing (task 114). Transcripts are synthetic.

checkpoints.description: Points where the player compares the debug.focus and debug.surfaces digests; two replays must give equal digests.

metrics.description: The result-v1 metrics the replay writes. name is a full-match regex over result-v1 metric names, as in scripts/perf-lab/stories.d.

compose.description: A soak story (task 122) that loops other corpus stories with idle gaps between them.

token.description: An identifier, number, flag or layout reference. No spaces, no slashes: never free text.

ref.description: An object of the layout snapshot by position, for example @w3.p0.t1 (workspace 3, pane 0, tab 1), since ids differ per replay.

blob.description: A content-addressed blob in R2 (perf-lab/corpus/sha256/<sha256>), fetched into the local cache.

file.description: A file in the repository (for example schemas/terminal-corpus/*.vt), at most 256 KB, with its digest.

payload.description: The input journal's key record (InputJournalEntry.Key) without characters. A typing key (letter, digit, punctuation, space, other without cmd or ctrl) has no key_code: the player types the next character of its fixed synthetic text.
The input journal's mouse record (InputJournalEntry.Mouse): window-local points from the top-left of the window, as debug.mouse takes them.
An action.run call: the action id and scalar arguments, each declared with its shape in schemas/perf/corpus-input-vocabulary-v1.json.
A call of the bundled cmux CLI, argv without the program; it must match a command of schemas/perf/corpus-input-vocabulary-v1.json.
